tier_definitions.name: LITE
tier_definitions.description: Basic non-math, non-programming requests needing little or no reasoning: greetings, small talk, short factual lookups, rewriting, summarizing, and everyday questions with known or simple answers.

tier_definitions.name: FLASH
tier_definitions.description: Direct instruction following and simple programming: straightforward code edits, short scripts, formatting, translation, data extraction, and ordinary tasks that are not math-heavy or deeply complex.

tier_definitions.name: PRO
tier_definitions.description: Somewhat complex programming, mathematics, problem solving, and complex brainstorming or exploration: multi-step reasoning, algorithm design, and debugging non-trivial code.

tier_definitions.name: ULTRA
tier_definitions.description: The highest-complexity reasoning: extremely hard problems, security vulnerability analysis, extreme problem solving, and very complex or system-level programming and architecture.
